observations: Only escapeText's comment/callback changes in runtime. All bytes beginning with CSS and all remaining renderer logic are preserved.

CR is encoded as the original character reference. A following LF suppresses the added br; a lone CR receives one br with no additional text node. Ampersand/angle/quote/apostrophe escaping and malformed-Unicode refusal are unchanged.

Arbitrary literal values are rendered as body text. The attribute use of escapeText is only the codec-generated pick-N key, whose vocabulary cannot contain CR; the new br cannot be inserted into an arbitrary-value attribute.

The existing model test changes one expected lone-CR HTML sequence. Its other original bytes remain exact. The appended five cases cover ordinary CR, CRLF, leading/trailing/consecutive CR, literal br/closing-tag text, and CRLF followed by CR across four displayed field types.
These authored tests prove markup strings, not visual browser line layout. The frozen independent DOM geometry and PDF span gates remain separate required evidence.
